podcast.title: TikTok-Generated Record Deals (2020)
podcast.body: By 2020, over 70 artists who gained prominence through TikTok had signed major label record deals. This demonstrates TikTok's power as a platform for new talent discovery and its direct impact on the traditional music industry's artist development pipeline. "But the time we got to 2020 over 70 artists from TikTok had signed major label record deals."

podcast.title: Book by Kalefa Sanneh on Soft Rock
podcast.body: Kalefa Sanneh's book *Major Labels* includes an argument that the term soft rock implies not merely restraint but also expansion, and that soft rock functions more as a fundamental "mode" within popular music rather than a strict genre. "Caliphus and A made this point in his book major labels."

podcast.title: Distribution Deals with Indie Labels
podcast.body: Major labels have distribution deals with many indie labels, allowing them to participate in the broader music market. "In many cases, these acts came from the world of indie labels who had distribution deals with the major labels."

podcast.title: Reduction to Three Companies
podcast.body: Over 25 years, the number of major labels was reduced to just three: Universal (the biggest), Sony, and Warner Music. "over the last 25 years their number has been whittled down to just three companies, the Universal, the biggest, Sony and Warner music."
